reason: The text explicitly describes the Hebrew people (represented by the assembly of Israel) approaching King Rehoboam with complaints about his father Solomon's heavy rule. Specifically, they state: 'Your father made our yoke heavy, and now you lighten the hard labor of your father and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve you' (וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת־ עֻלֵּ֑נוּ). Furthermore, when Rehoboam refuses to lighten the burden, the people explicitly rebel, saying 'What portion do we have in David?' (מַה־ לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜ד), demonstrating clear dissatisfaction with their leaders.
